title: SYSK Live: Koko, the Gorilla Who Talked
summary: Live recording at the Castro Theater in San Francisco about Koko the gorilla, the Western Lowland gorilla who learned American Sign Language at the Gorilla Foundation under Penny Patterson. The hosts cover Koko's birth at the San Francisco Zoo, her dysentery and move to Stanford, her vocabulary and jokes, her kitten All Ball, celebrity visits (Robin Williams, Mr. Rogers, William Shatner, Betty White), the AOL chat, the broader ape language experiments (Vicki, Washoe, Nim Chimpsky, Kanzi, Sue Savage-Rumbaugh), the scientific skeptic debate over anthropomorphism, the nipple-related lawsuit, and Koko's death in 2018. Interspersed with ad breaks and crowd banter.

segments.title: Opening banter and introduction to Koko
segments.summary: Hosts welcome the Castro Theater audience, joke about 1970s and 80s childhood, and introduce Koko the gorilla, born July 4, 1971 at the San Francisco Zoo.

segments.title: Koko's early life and move to Stanford
segments.summary: Koko had a difficult infancy, including dysentery and removal from her family. Penny Patterson, a Stanford grad student, took over her care and moved the project to Stanford, where Koko began learning sign language.

segments.title: Teaching sign language to Koko
segments.summary: Describes the molding and invitation teaching techniques, Koko's vocabulary growth compared with deaf and human children, and her move to a six-acre facility run by the Gorilla Foundation.

segments.title: Koko's jokes, lies, and insults
segments.summary: Examples of Koko's wordplay, such as calling a zebra a white tiger, the red towel joke, blaming Kate for a broken sink, and her made-up insult vocabulary.

segments.title: Michael the gorilla and All Ball the kitten
segments.summary: Michael joined the Gorilla Foundation and learned sign language, and the two signed to each other. Koko received a kitten named All Ball, who was later killed by a car.

segments.title: Celebrity visits to Koko
segments.summary: Celebrities who visited Koko, including William Shatner, Mr. Rogers, Fleetwood Mac and Sting, Peter Gabriel, Betty White, Leo DiCaprio, and Robin Williams, whose visit in 2001 was especially memorable. Koko's reaction to Robin Williams' death is described.

segments.title: Koko as ambassador for Earth and chimp anecdotes
segments.summary: Koko became an ambassador for the planet during the rise of the environmental movement. Her book, prints of her paintings, and an AOL online chat with a moderator relaying questions are discussed, along with questions about whether translations were accurate.

segments.title: Ape language experiments history
segments.summary: Overview of the ape language research field, including Vicki the chimp, Washoe and Loulis, Nim Chimpsky and Herbert Terrace, and Chantek. Noam Chomsky's language acquisition device idea is also covered.

segments.title: Anthropomorphism and the ape language wars
segments.summary: Explains anthropomorphism and the scientific divide between researchers who believe apes use language and skeptics. Describes researchers' efforts to avoid prompting, including Sue Savage-Rumbaugh's welding mask and the lexicon board used with bonobos Matata and Kanzi.

segments.title: Criticism of ape language research and later findings
segments.summary: Discusses edited video concerns, overstated mastery claims, the decline of ape sign language research since the 1980s, and 2017 theory-of-mind tests showing apes may have theory of mind.

segments.title: Koko's lawsuit, regrets, death, and legacy
segments.summary: Describes the lawsuit by former employees over Penny Patterson's requests regarding nudity, settled out of court; Koko's failed mating attempts; her death in June 2018 at age 46; and the 2014 symposium where many guerrilla researchers said Koko inspired them. Closes with Charles Hume's quote on animal welfare.

segments.title: Closing and credits
segments.summary: Hosts close the episode and the show credits are read.
